before.name: 2890 BC: Ancient Egypt: Pharaoh Qa'a died. End of First Dynasty, start of Second Dynasty. Pharaoh Hotepsekhemwy started to rule

after.name: c. 2890 BC: Egypt's dynastic transition; Qa'a and Hotepsekhemwy; dates debated

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The century page assigns Qa'a's death, the dynastic change, and Hotepsekhemwy's accession all to exactly 2890 without a separate citation. The Second Dynasty article uses c.2890, the linked biographies show other chronological possibilities and competing accounts of the succession, including possible intervening rulers. Qa'a's and Hotepsekhemwy's biographies cite a seal at Qa'a's tomb interpreted as indicating succession, but it does not give an exact accession or death year. This one-year slot is a reference for one approximate chronology, not proof any of these things happened in this year, an immediate succession, a continuous war, or a royal person's precise location. A broad Egyptian map point and radius are gameplay settings, not boundaries.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: One proposed approximate period transition; date and sequence debated.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Regional reference, not an attested location of individuals or transition.
